text: Message textarea (pristine): The Message field shows a red error border before the user has typed in it or submitted. This reads as an error and adds friction for a skeptical visitor. Expected after the fix: In the contact form component, apply the invalid border class and aria-invalid only when the field is touched (after blur) or after a submit attempt. Pristine fields keep the default outline border.

Contact page hero/intro section (desktop): On desktop the h1 'Book a consultation' starts about 4px below the header bottom (y=72 to 75), so it looks clipped and cramped. Phone has generous top space. Expected after the fix: Give the contact page container padding-top: 64px at the desktop breakpoint (≥1024px), matching the phone rhythm. Keep 48px between the intro block and the form card top, then align the form card's top with the h1's top.

Left intro column (desktop): Below the email line the left column is a ~550px empty void beside the long form, which makes the layout feel unbalanced. Expected after the fix: Make the intro column position: sticky with top: calc(var(--header-h) + 48px) and align-self: start. It then stays beside the form while the user scrolls. Copy is unchanged.

'What can we help with?' select: The select's text inset is ~20px on phone versus 15px on the inputs, and ~19px versus 15px on desktop. The text column is visibly misaligned in the form stack. Expected after the fix: In the contact form CSS, set the select to padding: 0 40px 0 16px with the same height, border and font-size as the text inputs. Use appearance: none with a 16px chevron background at right 16px so the text aligns with the input text.

Section separators and vertical padding (phone): On phone there is ~75px of space above the divider and ~75px below it before the 'TRAINING' eyebrow. The 'Typical engagement' line floats away from its own cards. Expected after the fix: On the services page at <768px, set section padding-block to 48px (was ~72px+). Give the 'Typical engagement' line margin-top: 16px under the card list.
